questions.question_text:
The mean weight of $9$ parcels is $6.4$ kg.
A tenth parcel weighing $6.4$ kg is added.
What happens to the mean weight?

options.why: Adds the new parcel to the total but still divides by $9$ parcels instead of $10$.
Divides the original total of $57.6$ kg by $10$ without including the new parcel's weight.
Adds the new weight to the mean instead of recalculating from the new total and count.

questions.solution_text:
$6.4 = 6.4$
The new weight is equal to the current mean, so it pulls the mean neither up nor down and the mean stays at $6.4$ kg.

Divides by the six members but forgets to add the extra $3$ hours to the total.
Adds the $3$ hours to the total but still divides by the original five members.

questions.question_text:
The weights, in kg, of five parcels are $2.6$, $3.0$, $3.4$, $4.0$ and $9.0$.
The parcel weighing $9.0$ kg is removed.
Find the new mean weight.

options.why: Gives the mean of all five parcels, before the heaviest one was removed.
Removes the $9.0$ kg from the total but still divides by five parcels instead of four.
Finds the median of the four remaining weights instead of their mean.

questions.question_text:
The ages, in years, of six members of a club are $21$, $23$, $24$, $26$, $29$ and $31$.
A new member aged $75$ years joins.
Find the new median age.

options.why: Gives the median of the original six ages, before the new member joined.
Counts the middle of the seven ordered ages as the fifth value rather than the fourth.
Finds the new mean, $229 \div 7$, instead of the new median.

questions.solution_text:
$21, 23, 24, 26, 29, 31, 75$
There are $7$ ages, so the median is the $4$th one.
$\text{Median} = 26\text{ years}$

questions.question_text:
The hours volunteered in one month by five members of a group were $6$, $9$, $11$, $14$ and $16$.
A sixth member volunteered $2$ hours.
Find the new range.

options.why: Gives the range of the original five values, before the sixth member was included.
States by how much the range increases rather than the new range itself.
Adds the new value to the largest value instead of subtracting the new smallest value.

questions.question_text:
The ages, in years, of six members of a club are $17$, $19$, $19$, $21$, $22$ and $22$.
A new member aged $22$ years joins.
What happens to the mode?

options.text: The mode stays as $19$ and $22$ years.
options.why: Assumes one new value cannot change the mode, but $22$ now occurs more often than $19$.
Keeps the smaller of the two tied ages instead of the age whose frequency increased.

options.text: The dataset no longer has a mode.
options.why: Treats a value occurring three times as cancelling the mode, when it makes $22$ the only mode.

questions.solution_text:
$17, 19, 19, 21, 22, 22, 22$
The age $22$ now occurs three times and $19$ occurs twice, so $22$ is the only most frequent age.
$\text{Mode} = 22\text{ years}$

questions.question_text:
The weights, in kg, of seven parcels are $1.6$, $1.8$, $2.0$, $2.2$, $2.4$, $2.6$ and $15.4$.
By how much do the mean and the median fall when the outlier of $15.4$ kg is removed?

options.text: The mean falls by $1.9$ kg and the median falls by $0.1$ kg.
The mean falls by $0.1$ kg and the median falls by $1.9$ kg.
options.why: Swaps the two measures; it is the median, not the mean, that barely moves when an outlier goes.

options.text: The mean falls by $1.9$ kg and the median does not change.
options.why: Assumes the median is completely unaffected, but with six values it becomes the mean of $2.0$ and $2.2$.

options.text: The mean falls by $13.3$ kg and the median falls by $0.1$ kg.
options.why: Subtracts the new mean from the removed weight, $15.4 - 2.1$, instead of comparing the two means.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{28.0}{7}$
$= 4.0\text{ kg}$
$\text{Median} = 2.2\text{ kg}$
$\overline{x} = \frac{12.6}{6}$
$= 2.1\text{ kg}$
$\text{Median} = \frac{2.0 + 2.2}{2}$
$= 2.1\text{ kg}$
The mean falls by $1.9$ kg and the median falls by $0.1$ kg.

questions.question_text:
A team of $4$ workers has a mean age of $30$ years, and a team of $24$ workers also has a mean age of $30$ years.
A worker aged $55$ years joins each team.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The small team's mean becomes $35$ years and the large team's mean becomes $31$ years.
The small team's mean becomes $31$ years and the large team's mean becomes $35$ years.
options.why: Swaps the teams; a larger group absorbs the new age more, so its mean moves less.

options.text: The small team's mean becomes $35$ years and the large team's mean becomes $35$ years.
options.why: Assumes one new value shifts every mean by the same amount, whatever the group size.

options.text: The small team's mean becomes $42.5$ years and the large team's mean becomes $42.5$ years.
options.why: Averages $30$ and $55$ instead of recalculating each mean from its new total.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{4 \times 30 + 55}{5}$
$= \frac{175}{5}$
$= 35\text{ years}$
$\overline{x} = \frac{24 \times 30 + 55}{25}$
$= \frac{775}{25}$
$= 31\text{ years}$
The small team's mean rises by $5$ years, but the large team's mean rises by only $1$ year.

It decreases from $7$ kg to $6$ kg.
options.why: Takes the middle column of the second graph as drawn instead of the middle of the ordered weights.
Assumes an extra value above all the others can never move the median.

options.text: It increases from $7$ kg to $8.4$ kg.
options.why: Finds the new mean, $42 \div 5$, rather than the new median.

questions.solution_text:

questions.question_text:
A group has $15$ members and the mean number of hours they volunteered is $12$.
A member who volunteered $12$ hours leaves and is replaced by a member who volunteers $27$ hours.
Find the new mean number of hours.

options.why: Treats the new member as an extra member, dividing by $16$ instead of replacing the member who left.
Averages the old mean and the new value instead of working from the group's total.
Assumes the mean cannot change because the number of members has stayed the same.
